Title: Tolvaptan in Later-Stage Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
Author: Torres et al.
Comment: Serious-adverse-event counts and reported percentages are based on the safety population (681 tolvaptan; 685 placebo). In accordance with the synthesis contract, group_1_total and group_2_total use the explicitly reported randomized denominators (683 and 687), while group_1_n/group_2_n and n_total preserve the safety-analysis population. The paper did not report an RR or 95% CI, so these fields are left null for downstream calculation.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Tolvaptan') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Phase 3 randomized-withdrawal, multicenter, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial
Topic of Content: Safety of tolvaptan in later-stage ADPKD
Participant type: Adults with later-stage autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with a serious adverse event during the 1-year double-blind period. Serious adverse events were defined as adverse events that were life-threatening or resulted in inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, persistent or clinically significant incapacity or substantial disruption of normal life functions, or a congenital anomaly or birth defect. Safety assessments were conducted monthly.
effect_direction: Lower risk favors V2R antagonist therapy
